args.rationale: Recurrent chylous right pleural effusion (triglycerides 434 mg/dL, lymphocyte-predominant, negative cytology) requiring repeat thoracentesis. CT shows bilateral hilar and mediastinal adenopathy with severe right middle lobe bronchial narrowing and partial atelectasis. The cause is unconfirmed (lymphoma, sarcoidosis, TB or other malignancy) and needs tissue diagnosis. The patient needs inpatient monitoring for re-accumulating effusion, and the work-up is incomplete because several tests were not available.
args.followup_or_handoff: Admit to medicine or pulmonology. Arrange EBUS-TBNA or bronchoscopy for tissue diagnosis, including cytology, flow cytometry and AFB/fungal cultures. Send serum labs (CBC, LDH, HIV, IGRA, ACE) as available. Consult oncology and thoracic surgery or IR for chylothorax management if the effusion recurs (chest tube, low-fat or MCT diet, octreotide, thoracic duct intervention). Monitor respiratory status and nutrition, and use airborne precautions until TB is excluded.
